epic.title: Build an extensible architecture for scientific paper representations

sizeLegend.M: roughly 3–5 focused solo days; re-estimate after design
sizeLegend.L: roughly 6–10 focused solo days; split into reviewable increments
sizeLegend.discovery: timebox a prototype/design before committing to implementation estimates
sizeLegend.external: depends on participant/expert availability, not only engineering time

issues.title: Define versioned research representation plans and execution contracts
issues.problem: A reader needs a faithful experience even when a paper does not describe an executable algorithm.
issues.scope: Define a representation plan over existing source anchors, assets, quantities, views, interactions, execution requirements and evidence. Provide small planning/build/execution/render interfaces with typed success, missing-data and unsupported results; retain v2 widgets through an adapter.
acceptance: Round-trip existing widget snapshots plus a biological process, physical model, algorithm trace, empirical result and theoretical argument through fixtures.
Keep source claims, pedagogical additions and requested execution level separate in the contract.
Plan/render callers do not branch on paper discipline; add two actual adapters before extracting a new seam.
Unknown versions and unavailable capabilities preserve the original record and return an actionable result.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

evidence.checks: npm run check: TypeScript, 218 tests, production build
evidence.browser: Native Chromium: guide step/quote, mobile source return with focus, widget-format import, unsupported-version recovery
evidence.limitations: Synthetic structural corpus; no new paid inference or independent scientific validation.

issues.title: Track evidence and provenance for every scientific representation
issues.problem: An attractive generated figure can silently present illustrative numbers as source measurements.
issues.scope: Extend existing fidelity checks to per-claim, per-dataset and per-view evidence records: source quotation, authored assumption, extracted observation, computed output and independently checked result. Keep conceptual, simplified, mechanism reproduction and experiment reproduction distinct.
acceptance: Every figure and exported artifact carries exact source/version, assumptions, evidence references and verification status.
Only application-owned checks can promote scientific labels; model self-assertions never do.
Changing a dataset, solver or generated artifact invalidates dependent verification while retaining prior evidence.
A mixed figure can label observed and synthetic series separately without replacing source claims.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

evidence.checks: npm run check: TypeScript, 223 tests, production build
evidence.browser: Native Chromium at 320 px: observed/illustrative data origins stay separate; a copied passed experiment report does not grant verification
evidence.limitations: Reference checker fixtures validate policy only; actual scientific reference checks are PP-108.

issues.title: Introduce typed scientific assets and inspectable data ingestion
issues.problem: Images, arrays and supplementary data cannot be represented reliably as loose numbers inside one widget.
issues.scope: Add bounded asset manifests for tables, tensors, images, sequences, graphs and geometry with shape, coordinate system, missing-value policy, units reference, origin, checksum and rights. Start with local JSON/CSV and existing original figures; extend formats through adapters.
acceptance: Import bounded JSON/CSV with a preview, missing-value explanation and explicit confirmation before binding data.
Detect shape errors, malformed files and oversized assets without losing reading state.
Separate user-supplied, source-extracted and illustrative data; record transformations and checksums.
Private assets and original paper bytes are not uploaded or included in public links automatically.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

evidence.checks: npm run check: TypeScript, 234 tests, production build
evidence.browser: Native Chromium at 320 px: CSV preview before binding, 001/null retention, export/reopen confirmation, malformed CSV recovery, 1000-row external dataset and wrong-checksum rejection; local table scrolling
evidence.limitations: Structural/integrity validation only. Specialized tensor/image/molecular renderers are subsequent issues; image references do not certify pixels.

issues.title: Model scientific quantities, dimensions and coordinate systems
issues.problem: A parameter that looks plausible may combine incompatible units or use the wrong axes.
issues.scope: Add a tested quantity/coordinate layer for scalar, vector, matrix and field data. Cover physical dimensions, explicit conversions, axis orientation and descriptive dimensionless quantities; use a dependency evaluation task rather than inventing a universal symbolic algebra system.
acceptance: Reference tests cover SI conversion, incompatible additions, affine temperatures and dimensionless probabilities.
Views and solvers declare expected units, shapes and coordinate systems; incompatible bindings fail before execution.
Units and uncertainty are shown in labels and portable records.
Legacy dimensionless programs retain their original arithmetic and descriptive unit limitations.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

evidence.checks: npm run check: TypeScript, 243 tests, production build
evidence.browser: Native Chromium at 320 px: 20 Celsius to 293.15 kelvin with standard uncertainty; declare cm without changing data, convert to m, reject seconds, export/reimport converted asset with nulls and transformation history
evidence.limitations: Finite SI catalog, IEEE-754 arithmetic; no arbitrary unit parser, frame rotation, field interpolation or covariance inference. Legacy AST semantics unchanged.

issues.title: Route plans through an extensible capability registry
issues.problem: Adding biology or physics should not require new discipline-specific branches throughout the reader.
issues.scope: Generalize the catalog into discoverable execution, data and view capabilities with versions, supported interactions, evidence requirements and resource budgets. Resolve a plan to available adapters and produce explicit capability gaps.
acceptance: The current widget catalog works as one adapter without rewriting its engines.
Register a second non-widget representation adapter through the same interface.
Selection uses required data/behavior rather than a discipline-name switch or model assurance.
Missing dependencies, offline operation and unavailable compute produce structured gaps and usable alternatives.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

evidence.checks: npm run check: TypeScript, 249 tests, production build
evidence.browser: Native Chromium: metadata discovery, behavior selection, unavailable ODE and evidence gaps, quantity/widget previews at 320 pixels
evidence.limitations: Trusted local adapters only; no generated-code execution, generic Muse planning or automatic scientific verification.

issues.title: Establish a cross-domain coverage corpus and unsupported cases
issues.problem: Animation demos alone cannot establish that an architecture works across research domains.
issues.scope: Build an attributed evaluation manifest of at least 12 real papers: four each in biology, physics and computer science, including empirical, theoretical and computational work. Include missing supplementary data, image-heavy extraction and cross-domain cases. Store links/metadata when redistribution is not permitted.
acceptance: Each case has an expert-reviewable concept, source anchors, expected representation level and required assets.
At least three cases intentionally lack enough data or compute for faithful simulation and have an explicit expected fallback.
Keep development examples separate from a frozen held-out subset.
Report corpus coverage by representation and evidence level; never describe twelve papers as universal scientific coverage.
issues.verification: Review source permissions and the case manifest; evaluate deterministic fixtures without claiming model runs or human reviews that did not occur.

evidence.checks: npm run check: TypeScript, 253 tests, production build; deterministic intake report
evidence.corpus: 12 real attributed papers; 4 per domain; frozen 8 development/4 held-out; 4 incomplete-input scenarios; metadata/links only
evidence.limitations: Source admission remains partial for two cases. Zero paper executions, independent scientific checks, expert reviews, model evaluations or human sessions in this intake.

issues.title: Build a composable scene and responsive layout language
issues.problem: Muse needs more than free-positioned shapes to create readable complex scientific figures.
issues.scope: Add nested panels, rows/grids, constraints, annotations, legends, repeated marks and semantic chart/scene slots. Separate scientific coordinates from responsive layout. Supply shared text measurement, spacing tokens and collision diagnostics; bound recursion and repeated elements.
acceptance: Render a biological process, physical scene and algorithm diagram through one layout contract.
At 320 px, 200% zoom and text-spacing overrides, no essential label is clipped; complex canvases offer explicit local scrolling.
Track objects across the whole animation so layout does not jump; report unresolved collisions rather than silently hiding information.
Enforce bounded nesting/mark counts and accessible numerical equivalents.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

evidence.checks: npm run check: TypeScript, 258 tests, production build
evidence.browser: Native Chromium at 320 px: local diagrams/tables, frame stability, collisions, source return; 200% text and expanded-spacing stress check
evidence.limitations: Synthetic structural examples; specialized semantic slots retain numerical fallbacks. Authored frames are not scientific simulation. Generic Muse generation and linked selections are later issues.

issues.title: Synchronize composed views through semantic interactions
issues.problem: A reader selecting a cell or time point needs every related view to reflect the same scientific event.
issues.scope: Extend the existing selection events to typed time, entity, spatial region, parameter and uncertainty selections. Compose a figure, curve, table and source annotation around one state store with adapters for existing widgets.
acceptance: A single selection updates at least three views and the source anchor without feedback loops.
Seeking, reset and undo preserve meaningful selection and distinguish input changes from view navigation.
A numerical fallback can drive the same selections by keyboard.
Snapshots restore linked selections without a model request.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

evidence.checks: npm run check: TypeScript, 265 tests, production build
evidence.browser: Native Chromium at 320 px: linked diagram/tables/source, reset/undo, portable entity+frame restoration, keyboard selection, legacy graph seek/edit/input undo; zero model requests
evidence.limitations: Coordinate-region protocol is ready for later spatial controls; specialized chart/image renderers remain subsequent work. Navigation digests grant no scientific trust.

issues.title: Represent processes, networks and state-machine explanations
issues.problem: Biological pathways, physical flows and algorithms share relationships that need more than a static node diagram.
issues.scope: Add directed networks, compartments, causal/process annotations and state-machine views using the composable scene. Distinguish authored explanatory transitions from computed execution events.
acceptance: One biological pathway and one algorithm state machine use the same structural renderer.
Support readable edge meaning, grouped entities and reversible selection with a relationship table.
Causal labels or reaction rates require declared evidence/assumptions; a drawn arrow does not establish causality.
Conceptual transitions remain labeled as walkthroughs rather than measured or executed traces.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

evidence.checks: npm run check: TypeScript, 269 tests, production build
evidence.browser: Native Chromium: biological process and state machine; active entities/edges, declared conditions/rates/guards, linked selection, exact source return; 320 px and 200% text/spacing; no dialog overflow or model requests
evidence.limitations: Authored teaching walkthroughs only. No reaction solver, guard interpreter, inferred causality or fake computed events. First-order rates support explicit Hz declarations only.

issues.title: Compose statistical charts with uncertainty and comparisons
issues.problem: Point estimates and attractive curves can hide uncertainty, scale choices and missing observations.
issues.scope: Provide linked line/scatter/bar/distribution views with uncertainty intervals, replicate grouping, explicit axes, log scales, missing-value handling and paired comparisons. Reuse current plots where appropriate.
acceptance: Render empirical biological and physical data with separately labeled observed, fitted and illustrative series.
Reference fixtures verify interval meaning, logarithmic-domain errors, missing values and consistent comparison scales.
Selections expose underlying values and sample counts; accessible tables preserve uncertainty fields.
A visual comparison cannot imply significance or a causal conclusion that was not calculated and justified.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

evidence.checks: npm run check: TypeScript, 277 tests, production build; pinned public-source extract and independent numerical references
evidence.browser: Native Chromium: real biological/physical data, linked values/source focus, log scales and recoverable invalid bars, computed histogram membership, keyboard selection, study export/reopen, generic embedded-data chart binding; 320 px and 200% text/spacing; zero model requests
evidence.limitations: Descriptive displays, fits and matched arithmetic only; no significance, causality, experiment reproduction or expert approval. Source uncertainties keep their supplied meaning; units are matched explicitly, never inferred or silently converted.

issues.title: Explore images, spatial fields and multiscale observations
issues.problem: Microscopy, simulation fields and spatial data need coordinate-aware exploration rather than a screenshot link.
issues.scope: Add bounded 2D image/field views with zoom, region selection, layers, scale bars and linked measurements. Keep source pixels distinct from segmentation, generated overlays and illustrative data.
acceptance: A microscopy-like image case and a physical scalar-field case share coordinate/selection contracts.
Image transforms preserve original coordinates and units; a linked table identifies selected regions.
Large or unavailable imagery has a bounded preview/fallback and does not block the reader.
Avoid fabricated image content, unverified segmentation and missing source/overlay attribution.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Support equations, proofs and experimental protocols without forcing simulation
issues.problem: Theoretical and observational papers may be better explained through a derivation, argument or protocol than an animation.
issues.scope: Compose source-linked equation transformations, proof/argument maps, protocol steps and annotated original figures. Link assumptions, definitions and evidence; retain original text and uncertainty about extraction.
acceptance: Provide a theoretical argument and an experimental protocol from the corpus without inventing an execution engine.
Distinguish authored explanatory steps from formal verification and source-reported procedures.
Every transformation/step has a source or an explicit added-assumption label and a return action.
Unsupported notation or missing protocol details remain visible and cannot be silently completed as fact.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Specify generated figure artifacts and a small authoring SDK
issues.problem: Muse cannot create a new interaction when every behavior must already exist in the fixed declarative grammar.
issues.scope: Define a versioned generated-artifact manifest: source mapping, entry point, data/state interfaces, capability requests, dependency lock, tests, provenance and resource policy. Offer a small drawing/control SDK and bridge existing declarative figures as a separate artifact kind.
acceptance: Document two working artifact implementations, declarative and generated, behind one build/run interface.
Generated artifacts carry explicit trust/evidence state and cannot grant themselves host privileges.
SDK fixtures demonstrate an interaction absent from the old custom runtime, such as manipulating a variable-length structure.
Record this planned scope expansion explicitly against CONTRIBUTING.md; generated code remains disabled until isolation gates pass.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Validate the isolation architecture for generated scientific code
issues.problem: Running model-authored code inside the application or an ordinary worker would expose the reader and server.
issues.scope: Run a bounded architecture spike comparing a separate-origin browser sandbox and a disposable server execution environment. Include compilation, rendering and numerical workloads; select adapters from primary documentation and adversarial measurements, not branding. Preserve application-owned controls outside untrusted output.
acceptance: Document trust boundaries and actual tests for parent DOM/cookies/storage, network, navigation, popups, downloads, nested workers, CPU, memory and message flooding.
Prove that cancelling or killing a hostile artifact keeps the reader usable and leaks no fixture secrets.
Specify platform prerequisites and unsupported cases; do not claim iframe, Worker, Node vm or a container alone is a complete sandbox.
Keep generation/execution disabled if the required guarantees cannot be demonstrated.
issues.verification: Primary-source design review plus repeatable adversarial prototypes in isolated test origins/environments; never execute untrusted code in the existing app process.

issues.title: Build reproducible generated artifacts in an isolated compiler
issues.problem: A syntactically valid model response is not a reproducible, loadable figure.
issues.scope: Implement the build adapter selected by the isolation spike. Resolve only reviewed pinned dependencies, disable install hooks and arbitrary build commands, emit content-addressed bundles and structured diagnostics under hard limits.
acceptance: Build a minimal SDK artifact reproducibly from an exact manifest and lockfile.
Reject undeclared imports, dynamic remote dependencies, malicious package hooks and filesystem escape attempts.
Bound build time, memory, log size and output bytes; cancellation cleans disposable state.
Store source, build diagnostics, dependency licenses and hashes without secrets or private source content in logs.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Host generated figures with a capability-limited execution bridge
issues.problem: A generated figure needs interaction and data without access to the rest of the application.
issues.scope: Implement the sandbox host selected by the spike and a typed bridge for immutable input, bounded outputs, selections and lifecycle events. Deliver only declared assets; prevent artifacts from launching inference or privileged requests.
acceptance: Run a generated interaction end to end in a real browser with host-owned attribution, close and stop controls.
Adversarial artifacts cannot access host data or escape the execution/network policy.
Validate origin, instance identity, schema, payload limits and message rate; isolate two simultaneous artifacts.
Cancellation, crash and resource exhaustion restore a readable fallback without losing notes or existing figures.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Let Muse plan, generate, test and repair new figure artifacts
issues.problem: A single JSON response cannot reliably produce a novel working scientific interaction.
issues.scope: Add an explicit generate-artifact action: Muse proposes a plan, writes against the SDK, receives bounded build/test diagnostics, and can repair within a fixed attempt/token/time budget. Keep existing catalog selection as the inexpensive first path.
acceptance: An unfamiliar mechanism can produce a new SDK-based interaction, build and preview it without manual code edits in the happy path.
All iterations retain the same source/evidence scope; failures and diagnostics are inspectable.
Set a maximum attempt count and a budget before creation; reserve each paid call and deduplicate accepted jobs.
Exhaustion returns a useful explanation or existing representation, never an unbounded repair loop or auto-accepted artifact.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Evaluate generated layout and interaction quality before presentation
issues.problem: A compiled artifact can still be unreadable, blank or unusable.
issues.scope: Create a deterministic visual/interaction test harness for the isolated preview with label clipping, overflow, touch targets, contrast, keyboard actions, reduced motion, console errors and post-interaction states. Feed actionable diagnostics into the bounded repair loop.
acceptance: Check 320 px and desktop layouts, large text, long labels, empty inputs, invalid values and multiple animation steps.
Detect intentionally broken fixtures: clipped label, unreachable control, blank scene and runaway animation.
Capture artifact/version, screenshots and failing steps; visual checks never substitute for scientific checks.
Host-owned error/stop UI remains accessible even when the artifact fails its own accessibility tests.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Cache and version artifact builds, executions and validation reports
issues.problem: Reopening an accepted figure must not regenerate different code or silently reuse results from changed data.
issues.scope: Extend portable experiment identity with artifact hash, SDK/runtime/dependency versions, asset checksums, parameters, seed and validation evidence. Cache separately at plan, build and execution levels.
acceptance: An identical accepted artifact reopens and replays without inference or rebuild when compatible.
A changed input, model-generated source, dependency or engine invalidates only relevant caches.
Unknown/incompatible versions preserve the original and offer export/fallback instead of destructive migration.
Recovery after interrupted generation/build/run does not start replacement paid work automatically.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Add a reference-tested adapter for differential and hybrid dynamics
issues.problem: Biological and physical models often require numerical integration beyond a hand-written scalar recurrence.
issues.scope: Implement a bounded trusted ODE adapter with declared solver, tolerances, initial conditions, units and event rules. Begin with small systems and explicit discontinuities; isolate richer solvers behind the same execution interface.
acceptance: Independent reference cases cover decay, a damped oscillator, a small coupled reaction system and an event-triggered transition.
Report numerical error/tolerance, instability, invalid domains and incomplete integration.
Parameter edits update linked trajectories locally and respect cancellation/resource budgets.
Name the supported solver/model class; do not advertise arbitrary ODE/PDE support or original experimental reproduction.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Add stochastic population and reaction-network experiments
issues.problem: Random biological processes need distributions across runs and declared assumptions, not one smooth deterministic curve.
issues.scope: Provide a bounded seeded stochastic event adapter for small reaction/population networks, including replicate summaries and a reusable process view. Keep teaching examples independent from organism-specific claims.
acceptance: Reference fixtures verify nonnegative counts, absorbing states, event-rate rules and deterministic seed replay.
Show multiple-run uncertainty separately from deterministic expectations and measurement uncertainty.
Reject incompatible rates/units, missing assumptions and excessive population/event counts.
A biological corpus example exposes its simplifications and source mapping without implying clinical or experimental prediction.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Add bounded physical fields and conservation-based examples
issues.problem: Physics papers often discuss spatial fields and conservation laws that scalar plots do not express.
issues.scope: Introduce a small reviewed field-model adapter for explicitly selected 1D/2D cases, boundary conditions, discretization and vector/scalar field output. Start with a narrow diffusion/wave or transport model after solver evaluation; no universal PDE solver promise.
acceptance: Independent analytic/reference cases verify the implemented model and applicable conservation or stability properties.
Grid resolution, boundary conditions, units, numerical scheme and validity limits are visible.
Field, probe and time-series views share selection and reproducible state.
Unstable settings, unsupported equations or excessive grids stop clearly and retain a source-linked fallback.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Explore molecular and structural geometry through reviewed adapters
issues.problem: Structural biology and chemistry need spatial geometry rather than a generic 2D schematic.
issues.scope: Add typed atom/bond/residue/geometry assets and a reviewed molecular/3D viewer adapter with labels, selection, clipping and a numerical/2D fallback. Evaluate format parsing and rendering dependencies during implementation.
acceptance: A small attributed structure loads with original identifiers and coordinate units preserved.
Selection links an entity to available source annotations and measurements.
Malformed structures, unsupported formats, excessive geometry and unavailable graphics have bounded recovery.
No inferred bond, fabricated structure, docking result or molecular-dynamics claim is presented as source evidence.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Execute discrete algorithms and variable-length structures
issues.problem: Computer-science papers often manipulate arrays, queues, trees or agents that the fixed scalar custom model cannot represent.
issues.scope: Add reviewed collection/event capabilities and a trace adapter with bounded arrays, maps, graphs, conditional steps and explicit operation counts. Use trusted engines or isolated generated artifacts according to the manifest.
acceptance: Two different algorithms beyond the existing preset engines execute on editable variable-length inputs.
Trace events map to source/pseudocode and expose intermediate structures, termination and operation metrics.
Independent reference/property tests catch incorrect output, invalid preconditions and excessive execution.
Conceptual pseudocode remains available when no checked executable implementation exists.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Explore empirical datasets, models and experimental outcomes
issues.problem: Many scientific papers report observations and fitted models rather than a mechanism to animate.
issues.scope: Build an evidence-aware dataset exploration path: select variables/groups, inspect missingness, replicate counts, transformations and a reviewed subset of fits/statistical summaries. Bind reported results to data/protocol only when actually available.
acceptance: An empirical corpus case is useful without inventing a simulation or unreported raw data.
Reported estimates, recomputed results and illustrative reconstructions remain separately labeled.
Reference tests cover supported fitting/statistical methods, uncertainty and invalid assumptions.
Unavailable raw data produces an annotated reported-result view rather than fabricated observations.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Define opt-in adapters for external datasets and heavy computation
issues.problem: Some papers require assets, trained weights or computation that cannot fit inside the browser.
issues.scope: Define a broker interface for reviewed data/compute adapters with explicit source/asset selection, upload disclosure, cost/resource budget, job lifecycle and returned evidence. Provide local-file and deterministic fake remote adapters first; infrastructure provisioning is separate release work.
acceptance: Missing weights, datasets or compute become named requirements in a capability-gap report.
External execution requires an explicit action and per-run budget; private data is never sent by local interaction.
Resume/cancel accepted jobs without duplicate paid creation and verify returned asset/result identity.
Generated artifacts cannot invoke the broker directly or select arbitrary external URLs/credentials.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Generalize the extraction and supplementary-material pathway
issues.problem: A domain-independent renderer still fails if equations, tables, microscopy figures or supplement references are lost during import.
issues.scope: Add an inspectable extraction-evidence manifest over text, equations, tables, original figures and supplementary references with confidence, original coordinates and user corrections. Reuse current PDF/arXiv extraction and extend through format adapters.
acceptance: Corpus cases retain relevant non-text material or explicitly record extraction loss and a return-to-original action.
Corrected extraction remains a versioned derived interpretation, never a silent source rewrite.
Follow supplement/dataset links only through explicit bounded retrieval with attribution and access checks.
Prohibit model-invented figures, equations or missing table values from entering the original-source layer.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Verify scientific behavior with independent references and invariants
issues.problem: Build success and model-generated tests do not establish scientific validity.
issues.scope: Implement a validation-report interface with independent reference cases, invariants, numerical tolerances, assumptions and verified scope. Treat generated tests as supplemental; distinguish a rendered example from checked mechanism/experiment reproduction.
acceptance: Intentionally wrong fixtures pass compilation but fail an independent scientific check.
Validation records identify what was checked, against which reference/data and with which tolerances.
Existing engines and one new biological/physical adapter share the reporting interface.
Evidence promotion and invalidation are application-owned and visible in the figure and exports.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Enforce responsive execution, cancellation and reproducible runs
issues.problem: Multiple rich figures can exhaust a browser or make the paper unreadable.
issues.scope: Provide a shared execution scheduler with per-artifact time/memory/result budgets, cancellation, visibility-aware scheduling and deterministic seed/version recording. Integrate trusted workers, sandbox hosts and optional external-job adapters.
acceptance: A stress fixture with multiple active views stays within documented measured budgets on a declared test environment.
Timeout, out-of-memory simulation, backgrounding and user stop leave the source/notes usable.
Replay distinguishes deterministic, stochastic seeded and hardware-dependent outputs.
No silent main-thread fallback or automatic paid inference occurs when an execution adapter is unavailable.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Provide faithful degradation and visible representation coverage
issues.problem: An unsupported paper should remain useful instead of receiving an unrelated generic animation.
issues.scope: Add coverage states by section/concept: represented, partially represented, missing data, missing capability and not applicable. Offer a justified annotated figure, concept map, derivation or protocol fallback when simulation is not grounded.
acceptance: Missing-data and unsupported corpus cases identify the exact unmet requirement and an actionable next step.
A reader can see which sections were analyzed and which claims remain unexplained.
Fallbacks preserve the original and never borrow an unrelated engine while implying execution of the paper.
Uncertainty is concise and readable; a gap can be exported as a bounded developer-extension request.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Retrieve relevant capabilities and control Muse generation budgets
issues.problem: Sending every solver, SDK example and domain recipe to Muse will grow cost and context without improving a particular figure.
issues.scope: Add bounded capability/example retrieval tied to a section/concept plan; keep a small common manifest and selected adapters. Account for planning, generation, tests and repair separately with explicit progress and ceilings.
acceptance: Record payload size and usage on the frozen corpus, including failures and unknown-domain cases.
A missing capability produces a gap instead of hallucinated SDK methods or packages.
Changing a slider, seeking, reopening or selecting an existing view never launches paid inference.
Cancellation, retries, deduplication and per-paper/global reservations remain effective across multi-step generation.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Share scientific experiences with complete reproducibility manifests
issues.problem: An exported figure loses its meaning if its data, runtime or verification history cannot be identified.
issues.scope: Extend study packs and snapshot formats for composed views, approved assets, generated-artifact hashes, engine versions, parameters, seeds and evidence reports. Preserve original rights and explicitly selected source inclusion.
acceptance: A fresh compatible browser can open an exported experience without regenerating it.
Unsupported runtime/dependency/data versions return a clear fallback and retain the original artifact.
Generated code executes only in the approved isolation host, including after import; portable HTML never bypasses that policy.
Secrets, provider job capabilities and unselected private data are excluded; attribution and asset availability remain explicit.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Run held-out cross-domain regression and artifact failure evaluations
issues.problem: The breadth claim needs measured successes and failures across domains, not selected screenshots.
issues.scope: Build an evaluation runner over the frozen corpus and adversarial artifacts: grounding, useful representation level, scientific checks, layout, accessibility, isolation, execution cost and unsupported behavior. Compare catalog-only and generated-artifact paths.
acceptance: Publish per-case outcomes, rejected attempts, missing capabilities and measured inference/resource cost.
Include biological, physical and computer-science cases plus empirical/theoretical and missing-data cases.
Use frozen fixtures in routine CI; separately named live Muse runs require explicit budget/opt-in and preserve actual outputs.
Regression criteria prevent silent evidence promotion, lost source anchors or weakened isolation.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Evaluate usefulness and scientific fidelity with domain readers
issues.problem: Agent walkthroughs cannot establish that a biologist, physicist or engineer learns from a representation.
issues.scope: Extend the existing real-reader study #24 with domain-specific interpretation and misleading-output tasks. Separate domain-expert correctness review from student usability; keep the study pending while no participants are available.
acceptance: Prepare tasks and observation forms for biology, physics and computer science.
Ask participants to identify assumptions, distinguish observed from synthetic results and explain one changed parameter.
Record actual participants, limitations, confusion and misleading cases; do not invent sessions or replace them with model judgments.
Define and apply a revision/hold decision for scientifically misleading experiences before claiming broad usefulness.
issues.verification: Actual consented reader/expert observations when participants become available. Protocol preparation alone does not complete this issue.

issues.title: Document how to add a scientific domain without changing the reader
issues.problem: The architecture is extensible only if a new capability can be added through documented seams.
issues.scope: Provide an extension kit with manifest/schema, data adapter, optional execution adapter, view bindings, source/evidence mapping, resource policy and reference tests. Demonstrate a fourth-domain extension selected from the corpus gaps.
acceptance: Add one bounded chemistry, geoscience or astronomy example without new discipline branches in the reader/planner.
Document which parts are trusted application code and which may be generated and isolated.
Independent references, rights, unit conventions, unsupported behavior and accessible values accompany the example.
A clean installation can run its provider-free fixture through the public module interfaces.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.

issues.title: Introduce the new architecture incrementally while preserving the current reader
issues.problem: An architecture expansion must not invalidate saved papers and existing accepted figures.
issues.scope: Roll out contracts, composed views and isolated artifacts through explicit capability/version gates. Keep current declarative widgets as the default fallback. This issue covers local product rollout and migration, not Railway provisioning or public release.
acceptance: Existing v1/v2 snapshots, saved Meta plans and local papers retain behavior or receive a non-destructive recovery path.
Generated execution remains off until isolation, quality and evidence gates pass; feature flags can disable it without losing source data.
A staged migration run records fixtures, cache invalidation, rollback and known incompatibilities.
Document completion evidence and separate pending human study #24 and release issues #31/#33/#34 from implemented features.
issues.verification: Deterministic integration/reference tests and a native-browser walkthrough; no paid inference in routine CI.
